what: Hilton franchises and manages hotels. It owns almost none of the roughly 9,000 properties carrying its brands; owners pay it a share of room revenue for the brand, the booking system and the Hilton Honors loyalty programme.
customers: Hotel owners and developers paying fees, and travellers booking through its brands.
money: a percentage of room revenue plus loyalty and credit-card fees
running hotels on behalf of owners
moat: A loyalty programme with hundreds of millions of members that fills rooms, which is why owners choose its flags over independent operation.
risks: Travel demand falls sharply in a recession
US hotel pricing has flattened after the post-pandemic recovery
Owners can move to a competing brand at contract renewal
New hotel construction slows when financing is expensive
opportunities: Asset-light economics give a return on capital near 24% with little investment
The development pipeline adds rooms and fees funded by other people's capital
Credit-card and loyalty revenue is stable and growing
watch: Net unit growth and revenue per available room.
